articles.title: Atletico Madrid release furious Julian Alvarez statement amid Arsenal interest
articles.summary: Atletico claimed they are the ‘victims’ in the transfer saga after Alvarez was booed by supporters on Sunday amid interest from Barcelona and Arsenal
articles.body:
Atletico Madrid insisted there is "zero per cent chance" they sell Julian Alvarez to Barcelona this summer and claim they are "the only victims" in the protracted transfer saga.

The 26-year-old forward has made it clear that he would like to join Barcelona but Arsenal continue to monitor the situation and may move to make a late deal for the Argentina international.

The Independent understands that Atletico would like Alvarez's future to be decided by Friday. The forward was booed during a substitute appearance in Atletico's draw with Villarreal on Sunday night and reportedly missed training on Wednesday, which the club put down to "illness".

Atletico have made it clear throughout the summer that they do not want to sell Alvarez, who is under contract until 2030. The Independent reported earlier on Wednesday that Atletico could listen to offers for around €150m (£128m) but don't believe Barcelona have the budget.

After Barcelona president Joan Laporta confirmed his club's interest in Alvarez and urged Atletico to accept their offer, Atletico released a furious statement on Wednesday accusing Barcelona and Alvarez's representatives of creating a "campaign of lies and half-truths".

"The player is being portrayed as a victim, but the only victims in the Julian case are us," Atletico told Spanish outlet Marca . "They have harmed us economically and socially. There is zero per cent chance of selling him to Barca."

Marca reported that Atletico claimed the Alvaraz saga "is not about money, it is about dignity". The club added: "A campaign has been created with many lies and half-truths. The only one who pays for this is Atletico."

There is one week to go until the transfer deadline closes and so far Barcelona's only offer for Alvarez was tabled at €100m (£86m). Atletico want Alvarez to be fit for their trip to Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday evening.

Arsenal continue to work on a deal for Alvarez despite their understanding that the player's preference is to join Barcelona. They believe Atletico could yet sell Alvarez if they receive an acceptable offer by the end of the week.

The Independent reported that Arsenal could offer Atletico another forward as part of a deal, such as Viktor Gyokeres or Gabriel Jesus , with Mikel Arteta keen to build his attack around the former Manchester City attacker.

articles.title: Another season, another failure - where did it all go wrong for Celtic?
articles.summary: Celtic have now faltered in Champions League qualifying on six successive occasions. What are the ramifications this time?
articles.body:
Six attempts to qualify for the Champions League in the past eight years. Six successive failures. And a sixth post-mortem for Celtic.

Picking through the wreckage of a European campaign has become almost an August perennial when it comes to the Scottish champions. But few of those failures have been quite so wretched as this one.

Leading 3-0 from the first leg in Glasgow, Celtic took the lead in Austria . Three quarters through the two-legged tie, they still held a three-goal advantage. But then came the collapse.

Ultimately, it took until the 90th-minute of the second leg for LASK to level the tie 4-4 on aggregate, but it would be hard to say it wasn't coming after a second-half bombardment in Linz. The hosts' fifth goal - the winner - was inevitable.

Martin O'Neill's side had won all four competitive games to start the season, scoring 13 goals in the process. Everything was rosey. But now the questions are piling up.

What's the problem with this Celtic squad?

Captain Callum McGregor said Celtic looked "scared" and were "passive" as LASK launched wave upon wave of attacks as the game went on in Linz.

Benjamin Nygren, Auston Trusty and Luke McCowan all made errors that led directly to concessions and Celtic simply did not compete in midfield.

Martin O'Neill insisted he was responsible, but former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes the manager was just protecting his players.

"I feel for Martin because he's taking full responsibility," Brown told BBC Scotland .

"I've been in Martin's situation. When you get humiliated in a game, you need to take that pressure off the players because in a week's time they've got another game."

Celtic's defence at full-time consisted of third-choice right-back Anthony Ralston , Trusty - who did not train in the build-up because of illness - untested academy product Dane Murray , and Liam Scales out of position at left-back.

Brown says Celtic's depth isn't of the level required to compete in Europe's premier club competition.

"The substitutes aren't Martin's players," he added. "The strength and depth in areas still needs a little bit of quality because the players that came on didn't hit the same level as the ones that went off."

Celtic have bought forwards Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran for big money this summer, as well as signing midfielder Mika Baur and winger Haissem Hassan .

However, they have sold key players Daizen Maeda and Arne Engels to Ipswich Town and West Ham United , respectively.

Former Celtic striker Chris Sutton questioned the decision to let influential players leave before such a crucial game on social media, while Brown says Engels' absence was a telling factor on the night.

"What they're missing is probably another physical centre midfielder that can be alongside [McGregor] in there to help him out," he added.

"Because Arne Engels is a huge miss physically, not just for the battle, but his legs and running power as well, getting in behind, but his mentality as well."

How much will Champions League exit cost Celtic?

When Celtic reached the Champions League play-off round before losing to Bayern Munich in 20024/25, their revenue of £143m ranked them among the top 60 clubs in Europe that year.

The same season, Ipswich Town had the lowest revenue of any English Premier League club at £155m. It's perhaps also worth considering, though, that the last published LASK turnover was only £42m.

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire estimates the financial consequences of failing to make it to the Champions League this term will be north of £20m.

"For every £100 generated in the Champions League in terms of prize money, it works out at about £22 in the Europa League and about £11 in the Conference League," Maguire told BBC Sport Scotland.

"Celtic made about £45m in season 2024-25 when they got to the Champions League knockout play-off - that's total prize money, including the SPFL money, but it's still indicative of how successful the competition can be.

" Aston Villa , who won the Europa League last year, probably made somewhere in the region of £30-35m and at least they have the benefit of automatically qualifying for the Champions League.

"It is a blow for Celtic. If you look at their share price today, it is down about 4-5%, reflecting that impact on future revenues."

Celtic charged £44 more for an adult four-match Champions League package two years ago than they did for the subsequent Europa League campaign. The difference in hospitality packages was even greater.

O'Neill spoke about transfer targets having to be reassessed in the wake of the defeat and Maguire pointing out that the club will likely lose out on sponsor bonuses, too.

"Celtic's fans will buy tickets whether it's Real Madrid or Raith Rovers, but in terms of the prices that can be charged - especially for corporate and hospitality - it's a licence to name your own price when big European clubs come to town."

Gerry : Callum McGregor says we'll now see what people are made of. Bit late. Should have said that after we gifted LASK their first goal. We are not a Champions League club. Simple. The board are a shambles and responsible for the club's failures again and again.

Eamonn : Shocking but not surprised. The squad is the accumulation of four or five disastrous windows. Four recent signings weren't going to fix that.

Martin : We are a club that have a board that wait until we get into the Champions League before spending any meaningful cash when we actually need a board that spends meaningful cash to ensure we have the best possible chance of negotiating these horrible qualifiers. Celtic were dead on their feet at the end - one of the worst results and performances in our modern history.

Patrick : Viljami Sinisalo is the only player who showed up, everyone else was a passenger. Reo Hatate and Luke McCowan should be kicked out the door. Another year, another wasted effort. What a terrible loss. The fans deserve better - the players, the board, the club are fortunate to be where they are. Odds on Martin O'Neill gone by Christmas?

Danny : Heartbreaking loss. Players didn't show up. Sinisalo was great, but our lack of depth and quality was harshly exposed. We scored some screamers last week and got away with a couple. Reality came back to bite us. Credit to LASK.

Paul : Fell short again. Playing like that, it's probably best we're not in the Champions League. McCowan should never get another game for Celtic. Sebastian Tounekti , Yang Hyun-jun and Anthony Ralston should be told to find another club. Martin O'Neill needs to take his share of the blame for this. Team didn't know whether to go for it or defend.

What are wider consequences for Scottish game?

Scotland being ranked as high as ninth in Uefa's coefficient table seems a world away right now. What might surprise many is that it was between 2021 and 2023.

This coefficient table determines how many places each country gets in the three European competitions.

With that ninth place came a guaranteed place in the Champions League proper for the Premiership champions, and the runners-up only had two qualifying rounds to navigate in the same competition.

But such has been the sharp decline since then that Scotland are now 18th, and this season's title winners will start in the second qualifying round of the Champions League, with the runners-up in the Conference League.

Celtic's capitulation at the hands of LASK underlined that decline. But it is not terminal for the country's position in the coefficient table.

When Celtic made the Champions League knockout play-off round in 2024-25, they scored 17.70 points. Yet Rangers scored more points - 19.750 - by reaching the last 16 of the Europa League.

So, with Celtic now in the Europa League, it can still be a positive.

In the live coefficient table - taking into account this season - Scotland have already dropped to 19th and there is no danger of losing further places.

But Scotland's hopes of climbing back up would damaged if Rangers, Hibernian and Motherwell fail to make it through to the Conference League on Thursday.

Returning to the top 15 should be the immediate aim, as that gets the runners-up back into the Champions League.

articles.title: Former Premier League star 'reported missing' in Budapest as police begin search
articles.summary: Akos Buzsaky, the former Queens Park Rangers and Portsmouth midfielder who earned 20 caps for Hungary, has been reported missing in Budapest since August 18
articles.body:
Hungarian authorities are searching for former Queens Park Rangers and Portsmouth player Akos Buzsaky. The 44-year-old has been unaccounted for since August 18 in Budapest, leading police to issue a public appeal for information.

Buzsaky represented Hungary 20 times as a midfielder and featured for Plymouth, QPR, Portsmouth, and Barnsley throughout his playing days. He recorded 18 Premier League appearances, registering two goals and two assists, via The Mirror .

QPR released a statement saying: "The club are concerned to learn that R's favourite Akos Buzsaky has been reported missing. We're all praying he's found safe and well."

Plymouth responded: "We are concerned to hear that Akos Buzsáky has been reported missing. Everybody at Plymouth Argyle is hoping that Akos is found safe soon."

The midfielder hung up his boots in 2015 following a spell back in Hungary with Ferencvaros and, according to his father, has been operating as a construction contractor in recent years.

Authorities have not disclosed the reason behind their search for Buzsaky. His father, Akos Buzsaky Sr told Hungarian publication Blikk: "I didn't know that the police were also looking for my son.

"He basically spends a lot of time in Greece, where he works as a construction contractor. He spent almost the entire last year there.

"Since we don't live under the same roof, it's not surprising that we only speak less often. The last time I spoke to him was last week, when he was at home."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Buzsaky has openly addressed his battles with addiction following his retirement from professional soccer. "I found a source of joy in life that I became addicted to," he said on a podcast.

"What addictions are there: gambling, alcohol, drugs. I fell into one of them, which I am not proud of. It is a part of my life, if I were to deny it or declare that period as not having happened, I would be deceiving myself."

Buzsaky began his professional journey at MTK Budapest before transferring to FC Porto in 2002 during José Mourinho's tenure as manager. His path eventually led him to England, where he initially joined Plymouth on a temporary deal in 2005 before making his way to QPR.

The Hungary international secured a permanent move to the West London club in 2008 after an impressive loan stint. He remained with QPR for four years, recording 125 appearances with 24 goals and 13 assists during what proved to be the most stable chapter of his playing days.

articles.title: QB battle is too close to call for CBA football, so the Brothers will play both
articles.summary: CBA seeks a sixth straight Super Bowl appearance this fall.
articles.body:
COLONIE - Since Bobby Burns took over as the football coach at Christian Brothers Academy in 2021, he's had a quarterback named Jones leading the way for the Brothers when it came time to compete in the Class AA sectionals.

That luxury is no longer afforded to CBA this year.

Archie Jones, who served as a full-time starter in 2024 and 2025, has graduated. Before that, Donnie Jones took over as quarterback to start the 2021 playoffs, and shared the job in 2023 with his younger brother and Jake Iacobaccio. During that five-season span, CBA reached the Super Bowl each time and won the first four of those games before suffering a 14-13 setback against Saratoga Springs in the 2025 Class AA Super Bowl.

This season, senior Matt Kowalski and sophomore Leo Field will be handling the quarterback position for CBA. As the Brothers prepare for their season opener Sept. 4 at home against Archbishop Stepinac, Burns plans to use both quarterbacks.

"They are both going to play. They have different skill sets. Leo can see everything because he is bigger and a little more statuesque. Matt is more athletic," Burns said. "These are two kids that have busted their tails for eight months. ... I may start one of them and, after two series, we may need a spark and the other one is in. They both have to know I have the confidence in them to do what needs to be done."

"We are definitely going to be pushing each other as much as we can," said Kowalski, who is from Latham.

"We are trying to compete each day and push each other," said Field, an Albany native. "When I am in, I take the physical reps. When Matt is in, I take the mental reps. I am trying each day to learn the offense and get better."

Kowalski is more of a running threat than Field, but he can also get the ball down the field as a passer. Field is more of the traditional pocket passer.

CBA has won sectional titles using more than one quarterback. At this point, Burns said the competition between the two quarterbacks is too close to definitively select one over the other.

"Matt Kowalski, from where he was at the end of last season to now, has made as much progress as anyone in the program. I am not taking anything from Leo in saying that. Leo has more natural quarterback ability than Matt, but Matt is a great athlete playing quarterback," Burns said.

Both quarterbacks are excited for the chance to play a role for the Brothers, who should be a top Section 2 contender once again.

"I have a lot to live up to with the quarterbacks we've had and their work ethic," Kowalski said. "I am stoked. I am really trying to show what I can do and what our receivers, running backs and linemen can do as a team."

"We've got studs," Field said. "We have a bunch of playmakers all over the field. One-on-one, we have guys that can compete with anybody in the state. We just have to give them a chance. That is what coach Burns says all the time: 'Give them a chance.'"

Both Kowalski and Field know just how motivated all the returning players are to reclaim the top spot in Class AA. The championship loss against Saratoga Springs still stings.

"This is a team with big expectations," Field said.

"It was really unfortunate and heartbreaking to lose to Saratoga. All we want to do is go out there and win," Kowalski said. "We have been preparing for a long time and we are ready to execute what we've been practicing. We are really motivated."

articles.title: El Cádiz irrumpe por Manuel Ángel y el Madrid baja a cuatro millones
articles.standfirst: Los avances con el Almería por el canterano se habían estancado por el precio del 50% del pase del jugador andaluz
articles.summary: Los avances con el Almería por el canterano se habían estancado por el precio del 50% del pase del jugador andaluz
articles.body: Manuel Ángel se entrena desde hace días en solitario a la espera de que su futuro se resuelva. El canterano del Real Madrid, que la pasada temporada debutó con el primer equipo teniendo espacio en Copa, Liga y Champions, espera que su futuro quede resuelto en breve. Eso parecía estar a punto a finales de la semana pasada, con el Almería como destino del Mami. Sin embargo, la cantidad que pedía el Madrid, seis millones de euros por el 50% del pase, se convirtió en un tira y afloja entre dos clubes que ya rozaron el año pasado en el traspaso de Rachad desde Almería al Castilla Con mercado y buenos informes en las secretarías técnicas de España, otros clubes han entrado en la batalla por Manuel Ángel al comprobar que lo que se daba por hecho, su llegada al Almería, no se cerraba. A la cabeza de ellos se ha colocado el Cádiz. El equipo que entrena Albert Celades ve en el centrocampista del Castilla una buena pieza para afrontar el regreso a Primera. Más si se lo quita a uno de los grandes candidatos, que es el caso del Almería. En ese tiempo, el Madrid ha rebajado a cuatro millones de euros la petición por la mitad de los derechos del jugador. Con el cierre del mercado, tanto la entidad madridista como el futbolista saben que la etapa en Valdebebas se ha cerrado y que la salida de Mami de la Casa Blanca es una necesidad para todas las partes. Eso no va de la mano con que el Madrid vaya a regalar a un jugador que ya tuvo espacio en su primera plantilla la temporada pasada. Manuel Ángel Morán Ibáñez, conocido futbolísticamente como Mami, nació en Albaida del Aljarafe (Sevilla) el 15 de marzo de 2004. Tras formarse en la cantera del Sevilla entre 2012 y 2018, puso rumbo a Valdebebas para incorporarse al Cadete B del Real Madrid. Desde entonces fue superando etapas hasta alcanzar el primer equipo, con el que la pasada temporada disputó siete partidos oficiales: uno de Copa del Rey, en el que debutó en Albacete; dos de Champions League ante el Manchester City; y cuatro de Liga frente a Celta, Elche, Mallorca y Betis

articles.title: La defensa de la Real podría ser ¡más joven que la del Sanse!
articles.standfirst: Si como parece el club txuriurdin incorpora a Mamadou Sarr y Héctor Fort, la media de edad de la zaga titular de Matarazzo sería menor que la de Jon Ansotegi
articles.summary: Si como parece el club txuriurdin incorpora a Mamadou Sarr y Héctor Fort, la media de edad de la zaga titular de Matarazzo sería menor que la de Jon Ansotegi
articles.body: Si como parece la Real Sociedad termina incorporando este verano a Mamadou Sarr y Héctor Fort, futbolistas de 21 y 20 años, respectivamente, el conjunto de Pellegrino Matarazzo podría presentar en algún partido una defensa más joven que la de su segundo equipo, tras el descenso al mismo de los ‘veteranos’ Jon Balda e Iñaki Rupérez. Sin duda alguna, un caso atípico y muy difícil de ver, por no decir imposible. La Real, de fichar a Mamadou Sarr, que este sábado cumplirá los 21 años, y a Héctor Fort, que tiene 20, podría alinear esta temporada 2026-27 algún día un cuarteto defensivo completado por Jon Martín, también de 20 años, y Sergio Gómez, que el próximo día 4 de septiembre alcanzará los 26. Entre todos sumarían 87 años, por lo que la media sería de 21,75 y podría ser más baja que la zaga llamada a ser habitualmente titular en el Sanse en LaLiga Hypermotion, que tendría una media de 22 años y medio, al acumular 90 Iñaki Rupérez (23), Luken Beitia (22), Kazunari Kita (21 años desde el próximo 16 de septiembre) y Jon Balda (24), que son los llamados a formar muchos días en el once inicial. Lo normal sería, como habrá sucedido siempre, que la defensa de la Real fuese de más edad que la del Sanse, pero el hecho de que el primer equipo pueda incorporar este verano a futbolistas muy jóvenes como Sarr y Héctor Fort, que se sumarían a Jon Martín, y que el club txuriurdin decidiera bajar al segundo a jugadores de 24 y 23 años, como Balda y Rupérez, podría provocar esta anomalía.

articles.title: Julián ve por primera vez que su única opción es el Arsenal
articles.standfirst: Asume por fin que el Atlético no le dejará salir al Barça
articles.summary: Asume por fin que el Atlético no le dejará salir al Barça
articles.body: El lunes, después de lo acontecido en el Metropolitano, Julián se dio cuenta, quizá por primera vez, de que no había otra opción que marcharse al Arsenal. Asumía, al fin, que el sueño del Barça no iba a ser posible... Se acabaron, de esta manera, los cantos de sirena de su agente sobre la opción de seguir su carrera en el Camp Nou. Sucedió horas después de un punto de inflexión que arrancó con una decisión poco habitual: Su familia no acudió al estadio como es habitual desde que llegó. Lo que pasó durante los 90 minutos dio otra vuelta de tuerca con el final, en el que el 19 se fue antes de que los compañeros llegaran al vestuario. La decisión de no exponerle con los ultras fue tomada por el club, como confirmó Simeone en rueda de prensa. Para seguir enredando la madeja, Julián no se presentó a entrenar este miércoles en el regreso al trabajo tras comunicarse con el club por la mañana para decirles que había pasado mala noche y no estaba en condiciones de completar la sesión de entrenamiento complicando todavía más la única opción que se veía en el club de que se pudiera reconducir: que pidiera perdón y romper con su agente. Durante los últimos días, Julián está más acompañado por Sergio, el segundo de sus agentes, que por el citado Hidalgo, que se ha quedado en un segundo plano mientras todo lo que va sucediendo cerca de la figura de la Araña le invita a pensar por primera vez en una salida… rumbo al Arsenal. El mercado se agota, la postura de no venderle al Barça se mantiene en el mismo punto inflexible y que la gente respondiera como lo hizo en el Metropolitano el pasado domingo abre una puerta que hasta hace apenas unos días estaba cerrada a cal y canto. Veremos si hay tiempo para que la salida al culebrón Julián sea una marcha a Londres.

articles.summary: Flick está obligado a hacer un cambio
articles.body: El Barcelona recibe este jueves, a las 21.00 horas, en el Spotify Camp Nou al Athletic. El encuentro es el estreno liguero ante su grada del conjunto culé en la temporada 26-27. Hansi Flick mantendrá el bloque que se impuso con autoridad en Elche, aunque tiene que realizar un cambio obligado. Su lugar en el doble pivote lo ocupará Pedri. Pero el técnico alemán, además, ya podrá dar minutos a Rodri, el gran fichaje de la temporada en clave azulgrana. El centrocampista trabaja con el grupo desde el pasado lunes. El Athletic, por su parte, tiene las ausencias por lesión de Vivian y Prados, y la de Yuri por sanción. articles.standfirst: El actual seleccionador serbio estará pendiente de dos de los clubes más especiales en su carrera como futbolista
articles.summary: El actual seleccionador serbio estará pendiente de dos de los clubes más especiales en su carrera como futbolista
articles.body: Veljko Paunovic será una de las personas que más pendiente estará del duelo entre Getafe y Partizán. El actual seleccionador serbio conoce bien ambos clubes, después de haber vestido las camisetas de los dos a lo largo de su carrera y de mantener una relación especial con ambas entidades. Paunovic debutó con apenas 17 años con el Partizán, club en el que se formó y donde disputó 17 partidos y marcó dos goles. Poco después, su padre, Blagoje Paunovic, fue uno de los valodores de Veljo que, tras su buen hacer en Serbia, dio el salto al Atlético de Madrid en un momento especialmente complicado en los Balcanes. A partir de ahí comenzó una carrera deportiva ligada durante muchos años al fútbol español, pasando también por Oviedo, Mallorca, Almería, Tenerife y, por supesto, Getafe. En el conjunto azulón disputó 52 partidos y marcó 14 goles, además de formar parte del equipo que alcanzó la final de la Copa del Rey de 2006 frente al Sevilla. Una etapa que todavía guarda un lugar especial para el actual seleccionador serbio, que formó parte de ese primer Getafe que con Quique Sánchez Flores y Berd Schuster sembró las bases de la consolidación del equipo en la élite. Su vínculo con el Partizán también viene marcado por su familia. Su padre, Blagoje Paunovic, disputó cerca de 300 partidos durante sus diez temporadas en el club serbio. Posteriormente, también desarrolló parte de su carrera como entrenador en España, donde llegó a dirigir al Logroñés. Paunovic, además, mantiene una estrecha relación con el fútbol de su país. Cada dos meses aproximadamente realiza concentraciones con jugadores de la liga serbia que cuentan con proyección para llegar a la selección en un futuro. El seleccionador ha instaurado el mismo método de trabajo en todas las categorías de Serbia, con un código de comportamiento común para todos los jugadores y un mismo sistema de juego desde las categorías inferiores hasta la absoluta. Dos de los futbolistas del actual Partizán, Nikola Simic y Djurdjevic, estuvieron además en la última convocatoria de Serbia, el pasado mes de junio, una muestra del seguimiento que el extécnico del Real Oviedo y Chivas realiza sobre el talento del campeonato doméstico. Ahora, con el Getafe y el Partizán frente a frente, Paunovic vuelve a tener cerca dos clubes que forman parte de su historia. Una historia que comenzó en Belgrado, continuó en España y que ahora le lleva a mirar desde el banquillo hacia dos equipos que conoce muy bien.

articles.title: Jack Grealish transfer: Sunderland explore move for Manchester City winger with former loan side Everton still interested
articles.summary: Sunderland are exploring a late bid for Manchester City winger Jack Grealish; the 30-year-old spent last season on loan at Everton, who remain interested in bringing him back to the club
articles.body:
The Black Cats are keen on a loan for the 30-year-old, who has entered the final year of his contract.

However, a permanent deal is also under consideration as Sunderland look to strengthen in wide areas. They are also trying to sign Igor Paixao from Marseille.

Grealish spent last season on loan at Everton and they remain interested in the player.

He has been used as a substitute in City's Community Shield defeat to Arsenal and their Premier League opener against Bournemouth.

City no longer have Savio or Omar Marmoush available for selection after agreeing to sell the pair to Tottenham. Savio has completed his move while Marmoush is in the process of doing so.

This has left City short on options in wide forward areas for the time being, and has been exacerbated by a short-term calf injury for Jeremy Doku, which will keep him out for two to three weeks.

City are set to sign 22-year-old Brazilian Allan from Palmeiras as a replacement for Savio, but he is yet to complete his move. They are also interested in Cody Gakpo at Liverpool as they consider further additions.

However, as things stand, Enzo Maresca has Antoine Semenyo and Grealish as his only senior out-and-out wide options.

Both Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki have often been used there but are often deployed centrally.

Sunderland are also attempting to sign Igor Paixao from Marseille.

Regis Le Bris' side have firm interest in the player and submitted a bid for the Brazilian earlier this week. Leeds tried to sign Paixao last summer before he chose to join Marseille.

Talks continue to take place. Marseille need to raise funds and Sunderland's priority is to sign a winger.

Sunderland have also spent weeks in talks with Sporting Lisbon over Mozambique winger Geny Catamo. He has a release clause of £51.4m at the Portuguese club.
